summary:
**LUNARIS – Lunar Mission Intelligence & Landing Site Navigator**

Exploring the Moon is not just about reaching its surface; it is about knowing where to land, how long we can survive there, and whether we can stay connected with Earth. This is the challenge we aim to solve through LUNARIS.

We developed an interactive lunar mission planning platform that brings important scientific information together in one place. Using data from NASA/JPL Horizons, NASA Moon Trek and LOLA terrain datasets, LUNARIS helps users explore the Moon, visualize its surface in 2D and 3D, track the positions of the Sun and Earth, estimate solar power availability, and identify potential communication blackouts.

What makes LUNARIS useful is that users can compare different landing locations and mission dates instead of relying on separate tools and manually interpreting complex datasets.

Our goal is to make lunar mission planning simpler, more visual and more informed, helping researchers and future explorers make better decisions about where and when to land. We believe that better planning on Earth is an important step towards safer and more sustainable exploration of the Moon.
details:
LUNARIS – Lunar Mission Intelligence & Landing Site Navigator

LUNARIS is an interactive lunar mission planning and decision-support platform designed to make one of the biggest challenges of lunar exploration easier to understand: finding the right place and time to land on the Moon.

Landing near the lunar South Pole is particularly challenging. The Sun stays very close to the horizon, creating long shadows and periods with limited sunlight. At the same time, the Moon's terrain can obstruct communication between a lander or rover and Earth. A location that looks suitable on a map may therefore face serious power or communication difficulties during an actual mission.

I developed LUNARIS to bring these important factors together in one intuitive platform instead of requiring users to switch between multiple complex scientific tools.

Users can explore lunar locations, select mission dates, visualize the positions of the Sun and Earth, and examine how terrain affects sunlight and communication visibility. The platform combines lunar terrain information with celestial position data to help users understand operational conditions. It also provides tools for comparing candidate landing locations, exploring changes over time, viewing 3D terrain, and examining potential periods when sunlight and Earth communication are available simultaneously.

Technology and Data Used

LUNARIS was developed using React 18, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Three.js for its interactive frontend and 3D visualizations. The backend uses Python, FastAPI, NumPy, SciPy, Rasterio, and GDAL for scientific and geospatial processing.

The project integrates data and services from NASA/JPL, including the JPL Horizons API for celestial position calculations, NASA Moon Trek for lunar mapping, and NASA's Planetary Geodynamics Data Archive (PGDA) LOLA terrain products for elevation and topographic analysis. The current high-resolution terrain analysis focuses on the Faustini region.

What Makes LUNARIS Creative?

The main innovation is bringing terrain, sunlight, and Earth communication analysis into a single mission-planning experience. Instead of simply displaying a lunar map or showing the Sun's position, LUNARIS aims to explain how these factors interact at a particular location and time.

Its interactive 3D environment, synchronized mission timeline, terrain visualization, and site-comparison workflow make complex scientific information easier to explore. The goal is not just to show data, but to help users understand the trade-offs behind a mission-planning decision.

Benefits and Intended Impact

LUNARIS can help students, researchers, educators, and future lunar mission planners explore landing-site conditions more efficiently. It aims to reduce the effort involved in comparing locations and dates, improve awareness of potential illumination and communication constraints, and support more informed preliminary mission-planning decisions.

The larger vision is to make lunar exploration data more accessible and useful by turning complex scientific information into an understandable, interactive decision-support experience.

Factors Considered During Development

I considered scientific data sources, terrain characteristics, solar illumination, Earth visibility, mission timing, usability, and performance. I also focused on keeping the platform modular so that additional lunar datasets and candidate landing regions can be integrated in the future.

LUNARIS is a decision-support and exploration tool, not a replacement for official mission certification or engineering validation. Its purpose is to make the early stages of lunar site evaluation more accessible, visual, and evidence-oriented.
